bullets.title: S&P +1.2%, ISM Manufacturing hits 4-year high at 55.6 — broadest beat since May 2022
bullets.body: July ISM Manufacturing surged 2.3 ppts to 55.6%, beating MS forecast of 53.8 and consensus 53.9, with 83% of industries reporting growth, new orders at 56.7, and employment back in expansion for the first time since Oct 2023. Prices paid decelerated for a third consecutive month. S&P 500 futures were +0.6% to 7,564 with VIX at 15.62 and the index itself +1.2% to 7,577 intraday.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley calls early-to-mid cycle rotation: favor hyperscalers over semis
bullets.body: MS CIO Mike Wilson declares market transitioning from early to mid-cycle, rewarding high-quality earnings, stable margins, and AI adopters; hyperscalers outperformed semis by ~20% over the prior 4 weeks. AI adopters' net margins expanded 50bps in 3 months and are now 400bps above market average. MS sets S&P 500 year-end target at 8,000.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex ROIC signals positive; CY27 cloud growth revised to +29% y/y
bullets.body: Following AMZN/MSFT/GOOGL earnings (each +4-5% post-results; AMZN reaches $3T market cap), Morgan Stanley revised CY27 cloud capex growth to +29% y/y vs. +14% prior. Goldman's prime book showed the largest net US equity buying since November 2020 (+3.9 SDs), and global equities attracted $64B in the week ended July 29.

bullets.title: Goldman reshuffles Conviction List: adds MSFT and AMAT, removes AVGO and NOW
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs added Microsoft and Applied Materials to its US Conviction Buy list and removed Broadcom and ServiceNow. NOW traded +3.7% despite being removed. BofA separately reinstated RH and BBY at underperform.

bullets.title: Oil -6%+ on Iran de-escalation; airlines/cruise stocks rally
bullets.body: WTI crude fell ~6.7% to ~$79/bbl after Trump called off Iran strikes and opened talks, easing Strait of Hormuz risk (Hormuz crossings limited to 9/day; Iran still denies formal US negotiations). Airline and cruise stocks gained 2-3% on lower fuel costs. Brent crude fell 4.4% to $84/bbl.

bullets.title: US-Japan coordinate first yen intervention since 1998; BOJ deployed ~¥5.3T Friday
bullets.body: BOJ data suggests ~5.3 trillion yen in FX intervention on Friday; the US joined Japan in what analysts describe as the first coordinated yen-buying since 1998. JPM maintains USD/JPY forecasts at 160 (Q3) and 164 (Q4), noting that USD/JPY has decoupled from rate differentials since April 2025 as fiscal concerns and capital flows dominate. US Treasury reportedly has limited remaining liquid resources for further intervention.

bullets.title: Japan 2-year yield hits 30-year high above 1.57%; UK 10-year gilt -10bps to 4.95%
bullets.body: Japan's 2-year JGB yield surpassed 1.57%, a level not seen in over 30 years, constraining BOJ's ability to hike aggressively. Separately, UK gilts extended gains with the 10-year yield falling 10bps to 4.95% on broad fixed income strength.

bullets.title: Fed's Williams backs current policy stance; open to hikes if inflation stalls
bullets.body: NY Fed President Williams 'strongly' supported the latest FOMC decision, expects inflation to decline in 2H and continue falling in 2025/26, and is open to raising rates if progress stalls. He sees no financial stability risk from AI investment and called AI sector volatility 'unsurprising.' BNP Paribas forecasts three Fed hikes beginning December; Goldman warns reducing Fed communication clarity would raise market volatility.

bullets.title: Semis under pressure: memory selloff leads; software/cloud up 3-4%
bullets.body: Semiconductor sector broadly weaker in pre-market: WDC -4.4%, STX -4.3%, MU -4.1%, SNDK -3.9%, ALAB -3.6%, MRVL -3.4%. In contrast, software/cloud names rallied 3-4%: HUBS +4.0%, TEAM +3.9%, CRM +3.4%, SNOW +3.0%. JPM July recap noted US Tech -3.5% in July with Semis -22.9% and Memory -32.6%.

bullets.title: Open-weight AI models accelerate adoption via Jevons Paradox; NVDA wins in all scenarios
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Stephen Byrd argues open-weight models lower AI costs and expand addressable markets, benefiting NVDA and power infrastructure across all three model scenarios (closed/open/hybrid). 63% of enterprises already use open-weight models. Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max claims parity with Anthropic's top system; DeepSeek launched cheapest well-known model to run, reinforcing AI inference cost compression.

bullets.title: South Korea KOSPI down 31% from highs; volatility exceeds 2008 GFC levels
bullets.body: KOSPI fell another 3.6-5.1% overnight and is down ~31-40% from its highs, with volatility described as exceeding 2008 GFC levels. JPM noted Korea was down 34% intramonth in July amid severe deleveraging since mid-June.

bullets.title: AI inference costs collapsing; Goldman margin outlook seen as too optimistic
bullets.body: Token/inference costs are declining to early-2026 levels despite strong agentic AI demand, driven by Chinese competition. One analyst argues Goldman Sachs' margin forecasts for the AI/semi complex appear too optimistic given ongoing pricing compression.

bullets.title: July global PMI slips but holds expansion; PSC cuts 2027 world growth to 3.1%
bullets.body: PSC's foreign manufacturing PMI slipped 0.4 ppts m/m to 51.2% in July, still in expansion. China's private gauge showed slower expansion while the official PMI signaled contraction. PSC cut 2027 global growth from 3.3% to 3.1% citing the Hormuz energy shock; inflation remains sticky post-panic peaks.

bullets.title: Data center construction booming; broader non-residential construction stagnant
bullets.body: Data center construction accelerated 7% m/m and electric power construction hit a record high, both driven by AI infrastructure buildout. Computer and semiconductor construction declined 4.3% in June and manufacturing construction fell 1.2%, while private non-residential construction was flat in real terms.

bullets.title: Kevin Warsh nomination sparks emerging-market-style credibility shock — BofA
bullets.body: Bank of America characterized the market's reaction to the Kevin Warsh Fed nomination as resembling an emerging-market credibility shock, with back-end yields rising sharply (30-year reached 5.28% last week). Goldman warns that Warsh's unclear communication style and reduced policy guidance could increase market volatility and pricing errors.

bullets.title: UBS: July hiring stays soft; companies delaying headcount for AI efficiency gains
bullets.body: Street expects ~88k NFP adds in July, above June's 57k loss, but April-May combined payroll revised down ~74k. Federal employment is down 11.6% since Oct-24 peak; temporary help down 21.5% since March 2022. Companies are actively delaying headcount in pursuit of AI-fueled efficiency gains.

bullets.title: Section 301 tariffs lock in consumer margin tailwind through 1H27
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes Section 301 tariff rates lock effective rates at 12% for consumer baskets (vs 19% IEEPA prior) and 24% for softlines (vs 35%), delivering the strongest margin tailwind in 3Q26-1H27 before comparisons normalize. Policy seen as durable at 10-12.5% baseline.

bullets.title: S&P 500 Q2 earnings beat rate at record high; EPS far above long-term trend for first time since 1955
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank noted the S&P 500 Q2 earnings beat rate hit a record high, while a separate indicator showed EPS trading the furthest above its long-term trend channel since 1955. US earnings grew +20% YoY in July per JPM, with broad beats across sectors.

bullets.title: Pentagon plans AI data centers at military bases; CXMT eyes second DRAM fab in Beijing
bullets.body: The Pentagon is planning AI data centers across multiple military branches, adding a defense-demand layer to AI infrastructure buildout. China's CXMT is also planning a second DRAM fab in Beijing's Yizhuang district while already constructing facilities in Shanghai and Hefei — a potential longer-term competitive overhang for US memory suppliers.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz risk remains despite Iran talks; 3-5M bbl/day still flowing
bullets.body: Iran denied any formal US negotiations (talks with Oman only on shipping arrangements) and the IRGC claimed to shoot down a US MQ-9 drone. Hormuz crossings remained limited at 9/day as of Aug 2, but 3-5M bbl/day continue flowing via the southern Omani shipping lane. PSC lowered 2027 global growth to 3.1% partly on Hormuz energy shock risk.
